q-syn.label: Closest in meaning
q-syn.summary: One capitalised word; pick the option closest in meaning.

q-ant.label: Opposite in meaning
q-ant.summary: One capitalised word; pick the option opposite in meaning.

rules.text: A word is positive, negative or neutral in tone. Its synonyms share the tone, so options of the opposite tone can be dropped at once.
rules.bad: BENEVOLENT: malicious (negative) cannot be a synonym.

rules.text: In an antonym question the word's synonym is almost always one of the options as a trap. Find the meaning first, then choose the opposite, not the same.
rules.bad: SCARCE: rare means the same, so it is the trap.

q-syn.cue: 'Select the most appropriate synonym of the word' with one capitalised word.
q-syn.standard: Recall the meaning, then pick the option that could replace the word in a sentence without changing it.
q-syn.fast: Decide positive or negative first, drop options of the other tone, then choose among the rest.
q-syn.eliminate: An antonym is usually among the options, so drop the option that opposes the word before comparing the others.
traps: The antonym is almost always listed.
A word that merely fits the same topic is not a synonym.

q-ant.cue: 'Select the most appropriate antonym of the word' with one capitalised word.
q-ant.standard: Recall the meaning, then pick the option that says the reverse.
q-ant.fast: Spot and ignore the synonym trap, then pick the option of the opposite tone.
q-ant.eliminate: Cross out every option that is close in meaning to the word. What remains contains the answer.
traps: The synonym is nearly always listed as bait.
An unrelated word is not an antonym: the answer must reverse the meaning.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
BENEVOLENT
practice.why: Benevolent means kind and generous; charitable carries the same positive sense.

a.note: Malicious means wishing to harm: the opposite of benevolent, chosen by mistake when the tone is not checked.

c.note: Reluctant means unwilling; it says nothing about kindness or generosity.

d.note: Stingy means unwilling to give: it opposes benevolent, a classic antonym trap.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
FRUGAL
practice.why: Frugal means careful with money; thrifty says the same thing.

b.note: Lavish means spending freely: the antonym of frugal, placed as bait.

c.note: Greedy means wanting more than one needs; a frugal person is careful, not greedy.

d.note: Cheerful describes mood, not the way a person spends money.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
OBSOLETE
practice.why: Obsolete means no longer used because something newer has replaced it; outdated means the same.

a.note: Modern is the antonym of obsolete, chosen when the word is mixed up with its opposite.

c.note: Fragile means easily broken and has no link to being out of use.

d.note: Permanent means lasting for ever, which does not describe something that has gone out of use.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
VERBOSE
practice.why: Verbose means using more words than needed; wordy is the direct synonym.

a.note: Concise is the antonym of verbose: it means brief and to the point.

b.note: Silent means making no sound, the reverse of using many words.

d.note: Humorous means funny; a verbose speaker need not be funny.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
SCARCE
practice.why: Scarce means not available in enough quantity; plentiful means available in large quantity.

a.note: Rare is a synonym of scarce, which is why it is placed as the trap.

c.note: Limited is close in meaning to scarce, so it is a synonym-side trap, not the opposite.

d.note: Meagre means small in amount, the same side as scarce.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
EPHEMERAL
practice.why: Ephemeral means lasting a very short time; eternal means lasting for ever.

a.note: Fleeting is a synonym of ephemeral.

b.note: Transient is a synonym of ephemeral.

d.note: Brief is a synonym of ephemeral: it describes the same short duration.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
DILIGENT
practice.why: Diligent means steadily hardworking; lazy means unwilling to work.

a.note: Industrious is a synonym of diligent.

c.note: Careful describes attention to detail and is closer to diligent than to its opposite.

d.note: Eager means keen; it is not the opposite of working steadily.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
CANDID
practice.why: Candid means truthful and straightforward; devious means using indirect or dishonest means.

a.note: Frank is a synonym of candid.

b.note: Honest is a synonym of candid.

d.note: Open is a synonym of candid in the sense of being straightforward.
